questions.text: Consider a disk pack with 16 surfaces, 128 tracks per surface and 256 sectors per track. 512 bytes of data are stored in a bit serial manner in a sector. The capacity of the disk pack and the number of bits required to specify a particular sector in the disk are respectively:
questions.solution:
Capacity = [latex]16\times128\times256\times512=2^4\cdot2^7\cdot2^8\cdot2^9=2^{28}[/latex] bytes = 256 MB.

Number of sectors = [latex]2^4\cdot2^7\cdot2^8=2^{19}[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 19 bits to address a sector.

Answer: 256 Mbyte, 19 bits

questions.text: Consider a non-pipelined processor with a clock rate of 2.5 gigahertz and average cycles per instruction of four. The same processor is upgraded to a pipelined processor with five stages; but due to the internal pipeline delay, the clock speed is reduced to 2 gigahertz. Assume that there are no stalls in the pipeline. The speedup achieved in this pipelined processor is
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Non-pipelined: 4 cycles [latex]\times[/latex] (1/2.5 GHz = 0.4 ns) = 1.6 ns per instruction
- Pipelined, no stalls: 1 cycle [latex]\times[/latex] (1/2 GHz = 0.5 ns) = 0.5 ns per instruction

Speedup = 1.6 / 0.5 = 3.2

Answer: 3.2

questions.text:
A file system uses an in-memory cache to cache disk blocks.The miss rate of the cache is shown in the figure. The latency to read a block from the cache is 1 ms and to read a block from the disk is 10ms. Assume that the cost of checking whether a block exists in the cache is negligible. Available cache sizes are in multiples of 10MB.

The smallest cache size required to ensure an average read latency of less than 6ms is_________ MB.
questions.solution:
Average latency = (1 [latex]-[/latex] m) [latex]\times[/latex] 1 + m [latex]\times[/latex] 10 = 1 + 9m (m = miss rate). We need [latex]1+9m \lt 6\Rightarrow m \lt 0.556[/latex].

From the graph: 20 MB gives 60% (too high), 30 MB gives 40% [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] latency 1 + 3.6 = 4.6 ms True

Answer: 30

questions.text: Consider a 3GHz (gigahertz) processor with a three-stage pipeline and stage latencies [latex]\tau _{1}[/latex], [latex]\tau _{2}[/latex], and [latex]\tau _{3}[/latex] such that [latex]\tau _{1}=3\tau _{2}/4=2\tau _{3}[/latex]. If the longest pipeline stage is split into two pipeline stages of equal latency, the new frequency is _____GHz, ignoring delays in the pipeline registers.
questions.solution:
Let [latex]\tau_1=6k[/latex]: then [latex]\tau_2=8k[/latex] and [latex]\tau_3=3k[/latex]. The clock is set by the longest stage, 8k, at 3 GHz.

Split [latex]\tau_2[/latex] into two stages of 4k. Now the longest is [latex]\tau_1=6k[/latex].

New frequency [latex]=3\times\frac{8k}{6k}=4[/latex] GHz

Answer: 4
